pull.title: private broadcast: Extra guard against unintended non-private broadcast of private transactions
pull.body:
Motivation: Reduce the risk of accidental privacy leak happening when broadcasting non-privately a requested transaction that had been previously broadcast privately.

Background: During the initial phase of private broadcast implementation there were unforeseen instances when a private transaction could get broadcast non-privately (see #35032 #35319 #35410 #36309 #36312 #36277 #36330).

Currently known pathways:

- Re-submission through `submitpackage`
- Wallet-rebroadcast (when a private transaction is "picked up" by the wallet, and rebrodcast after 1-2 days)

Note that these are being addressed, but other, currently non-identified pathways cannot be excluded.

Change summary: Add a general, extra safeguard: whenever there is a transaction broadcast request, check if the given transaction has been previously broadcast privately, and if so, refuse to broadcast non-privately.

Transaction relay is not affected, as it should not be affected by private broadcast.  When we receive a previously private-broadcast transaction for the first time (it's not yet in our mempool), we relay it as any other relayed transaction. Behavior is unchanged in this regard.

Notes:

- Prerequisite: This is built on top of #36477, as keeping finished private broadcasts in the queue is a prerequisite for this change to work.
- This proposed change is not an alternative to the use-case specific safeguards, but a complementary one.
- Testing currently uses the two pathways listed above. When they are closed, testing will be more difficult (i.e., it is hard to establish whether non-private broadcast is prevented by the use-case specific or the present generic guard).
- The private broadcast queue is not persisted, it doesn't survive node restarts
- Entries deleted via `abortprivatebroadcast` will be forgotten.

Keeping as Draft, because the prerequisite #36477 is pending.

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first. ### LLM Linter (✨ experimental) Possible typos and grammar issues: - `test/functional/p2p_private_broadcast_then_public.py`: `privateproadcast-aware` → `private-broadcast-aware` [misspelling] 2026-11-02 11:36:49
CI failure: `TSan` fails. It may be related to the test pushing the mock time by 36 hours, which may affect some rate limiting. Investigating.

Attempted fix for "TSan" CI timeout.

Likely root cause: In the wallet resend part, node0's mocktime jumps 36 hours and then stays frozen. If node0's message handler processes the nodes[2] connection between the jump and the wallet resubmit, it resets that peer's inv trickle timer to the frozen time plus a random delay, so the timer never expires and the inv for the resent transaction is never sent.

Attempted fix: start node0 with `-whitelist=noban,out@127.0.0.1`, which gives its manual connections `noban` permission so they skip the trickle timer, as `wallet_resendwallettransactions.py` does via `noban_tx_relay`.

`git range-diff 7b2aae41d79624abc87198932d699ae77ec36323...0cd792580f01796d0ed16d9cf415f7b8a6ac5f20`

> Attempted fix: start node0 with `-whitelist=noban,out@127.0.0.1`, which gives its manual connections `noban` permission so they skip the trickle timer, as `wallet_resendwallettransactions.py` does via `noban_tx_relay`.

Haven't looked closely, but I wonder if this is the correct fix here. `wallet_resendwallettransactions.py` only cares about the day-long resend-delay, not the second-long trickle-delay, so it seems correct for that test. However, for the test here, either the test here cares about trickle-delay, in which case it would be cleaner to not use `noban` permission and instead make the test deterministic with syncs or so? Or, the test doesn't care about trickle delay, and can just set `noban_tx_relay` globally? Just wondering, up to you.

Thanks for chiming in! Indeed, the global `noban_tx_relay` seems to be a cleaner way.
I used LLM assistance for finding the failure reason, I've reviewed that it looks plausible, and reproduced locally (both with and without).
This test doesn't care about trickle delay, so disabling it globally is a simpler solution. Changed now.

author optout <13562139+optout21@users.noreply.github.com> 1792478243 +0200
committer optout21 <13562139+optout21@users.noreply.github.com> 1793618857 +0100

net_processing: don't announce privately broadcast txs on request

With -privatebroadcast, sendrawtransaction sends the transaction only
via short-lived private broadcast connections and does not add it to
the mempool. However, other code paths can later add the same
transaction to the mempool and announce it to all peers, which links
the transaction to this node:
- the submitpackage RPC
- the wallet, on commit and on its periodic resend (e.g. after the
  transaction came back from the network and was picked up by the
  wallet)
- the GUI PSBT broadcast
- ReattemptInitialBroadcast(), for transactions in the unbroadcast set

All of these end up in PeerManager::InitiateTxBroadcastToAll(), which
is also used to relay transactions received from peers. Add a reason
parameter to it (RELAY or REQUESTED). If the reason is not RELAY and
the transaction is known to the private broadcast storage, then do not
announce it, remove it from the mempool's unbroadcast set, so that it
is not retried, and log that.

Relaying a privately broadcast transaction after it was received back
from the network is not affected: at that point the node behaves like
any other node that received the transaction.

Extend p2p_private_broadcast_then_public.py to check that re-sending
a privately broadcast transaction via submitpackage or via the periodic
resend of the wallet does not reach a public peer, while another
transaction sent the same way does.
